scope: Semantic default-row Tabs extraction only; no product acceptance.

findings.problem: Semantic label extent loses the logical origin of each Display write under a left clip. It sums segment widths while RowUi::CellWriter advances from the logical content origin and clips each individual write. Repeated segments can overwrite earlier text at the clip edge. Consequently the semantic tab width, close cell, following-tab placement, and rendered styles differ from legacy drawing under the identical clip.
findings.reproducer: External consumer left_clipped_segmented: area Rect(0,0,30,3); clip Rect(5,0,20,3); closable(true); first Display emits write_str("ab"), write_str("cd"); second emits "next". Both runtime draws use ui.with_area(clip).
findings.requested_fix: Resolve semantic extents using the same per-write logical-origin/clipping semantics as CellWriter and paint_str, without painting or reading a buffer. Add a split-write left-clip regression comparing complete buffers and registered regions.

checks.note: Actual public-API external consumer; full Buffer equality, including cell styles. Normal split writes, vertically clipped row, and trailing wide-space cases pass; left-clipped split writes fail.

source_review.public_api: Existing Tabs constructors/state/update/row callback signatures preserved. New opt-in TabLayout stores owned text and keys; no second persistent component state owner. Committed receipt explicitly caller-owned. No unsafe code or new concurrency paths.
source_review.purity: layout_default does not accept Ui, execute update, register controls, or paint; it does call item Display once to own segments. Planned drawing formats only the owned DisplaySegments wrapper and does not invoke item Display.
source_review.compatibility: Legacy arbitrary RowFn path retained in shared draw loop. Native before/after suites both pass. This is not a lossless cross-revision full-frame proof for every legacy configuration.
source_review.author_tests: 106-test suite contains buffer/regions/cursor comparisons across four color profiles, widths 0/1/2/8/13/24/40, several reference focus/hover/press/close states, warm overflow receipt, segmented Unicode, stable-key reordering and custom RowFn. It never applies a nontrivial left clip, allowing this defect.
